Source: A 14-year-old boy presents to his pediatrician with a 2-month history of intermittent arm and leg spasms.
His temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 115/70 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, and respirations are 12/min.
Physical exam reveals a healthy child.
He has also noticed that they occur when he stays up late to cram last minute for exams.
He recently started experimenting with alcohol and marijuana that one of his friends has been stealing from their parents.
He says that the spasms usually occur after he wakes up as he is getting ready for school, and consist of disorganized jerking motions that stop after a few minutes.
